comments.text: Two inverse screen-code digits copied into the status display; Mystery Maze file variants share number25.
Initial placement-stream pointer consumed by resident $7514/$4D0F before the private initialization callback.
Background and border color bytes. Loader uses pristine backup $3804/$3805 when publishing VIC colors.
Seven-byte bomb record pointer. The scanner searches for key $FF; target count $3013 need not equal record count. PLF13 uniquely omits the terminator after its four intended records.
Four pending callback pointers copied by $758A into $40C8-$40CF. A zero high byte leaves the existing no-op task; nonzero vectors are committed by the resident IRQ.
Initial player X low, X high and Y in hardware sprite coordinates, read by spawn $56E0. This is the start of each life, not multicolor drawing coordinates.
Initial target counter 14. Collection decrements it; special bomb callbacks can compensate the decrement or replace the table. Primary record list has 14 entries.
Resident perimeter-bullet slot limit 0; $6800 considers sprite slots1 through limit-minus-one. Private level actors can use other slots.
Ordinary collection adds this little-endian binary value (100) to the24-bit total score. Private callbacks may add an extra award first.
Initial little-endian bonus 1500. The resident countdown subtracts100 per256 enabled IRQ services; completion adds the remaining amount to total and bonus records.
Private initialization routine called after initial scenery drawing. Common no-op target is the RTS at $301F.
Main-thread entry selected by JMP($301B) at $759C; typically the spawn/collection/exit loop at $3050.
Private cleanup hook copied into the local JSR trampoline before completion or exhaustion. A target of $301F returns immediately.
Shared one-byte RTS used by empty initialization, cleanup and individual bomb callbacks in this overlay.
Eight ladder/up-rope X columns followed by six down-rope X columns, copied to $40B0-$40BD. Coordinates use160-wide multicolor space; $FF marks unavailable columns.
Two zero header bytes between the climb-column arrays and completion vector; the shared loader does not read them as part of those arrays.
Ordinary successful-level destination $5B00. The private loop calls cleanup before jumping through this word.
Exhausted-lives destination $5FFD, the resident jump to game-over presentation $6A80. This is separate from successful completion.
Two filename suffix characters '06'. Resident loader copies them into $40D3/$40D4; private cleanup can replace them before the next disk request.
Single $FF drawing-stream terminator, used as the no-change post-bomb action.
Zero byte after the empty drawing terminator and before collection-key coordinate offsets.
X/Y offsets applied by resident $55BF when reducing player position to the bomb lookup key. They adjust the coarse cell test, not the visible bomb positions.
Optional hook called before the matched bomb-record callback. A zero high byte suppresses the call; otherwise the resident patches JSR $5643 from this word.
Twenty loaded zero bytes align the private main loop to $3050. Header fields end at $303B; no private structure is assigned to this gap.

Spawn/reveal a life through $436A, then repeatedly check bomb collection through $436D. Zero remaining count at $3013 exits through success vector $3030 after setting divisor 9; death state $4028=2 waits for state 0, then respawns unless lives sentinel $40E4=$FF, which exits through $3032. Both exits call the header cleanup pointer.

Patch local JSR operand from little-endian header $301D/$301E, invoke cleanup, return. In this file the header resolves to shared no-op RTS at $301F; the assembled $FFFF target is a placeholder, not a real call.
Fourth IRQ callback requests death 1 on a nonzero player collision shadow while state 0 and nonzero $402B.

Drawing data $30A4-$3155 read by Initial scenery $30A4. Stream commands are FE shape pointer, FD repeat delta, FC stream jump, x/y/count placement and FF end. Referenced shapes hold width/x-offset/y-offset/pixel rows endingFF; source pixel codes are0 background,1 bomb,2 support,3 climbable. Parsed by the same behavioral renderer checked against original $4D0F.

14 seven-byte records [coarse key,x,y,callback low/high,post-draw low/high]. Terminator: $FF. Coordinates are160-wide bitmap positions. The resident scanner matches the key, calls both hooks, adds $3015 points, erases the bomb, follows the draw pointer and decrements $3013. This list is not bounded by the target counter.

Drawing data $31B9-$31D6 read by Post-bomb drawing $31B9, Post-bomb drawing $31C3, Post-bomb drawing $31CD. Stream commands are FE shape pointer, FD repeat delta, FC stream jump, x/y/count placement and FF end. Referenced shapes hold width/x-offset/y-offset/pixel rows endingFF; source pixel codes are0 background,1 bomb,2 support,3 climbable. Parsed by the same behavioral renderer checked against original $4D0F.
Eight compact 30-byte frames,240 bytes, expanded to $8400-$85FF. Animated hunter uses sequence 10,11,12,13,14,15,12,16; slot 17 is the initial dormant pose.
Expand private frames, initialize sprites 1..3 colour 12 and X161/193/177, Y66/66/64, X-high 0, pointer 17 and enabled 1. They remain in dormant poses until bomb callbacks activate them.

Every bomb record points here. Increment modulo 3 count $3455; each third bomb increments active count $3454 up to 3 and changes newly activated sprite frame to 10. Further collections leave active count capped 3.
Third callback returns when activecount 0, deathstate 2 or divisor $4029>=9. Otherwise accumulate six-callback divider $346A; on sixth update calculate player half-X and enter hunter loop.

For each active hunter save its pre-move half-X, add signed 16-bit X and 8-bit Y velocity, wrap bottomY>=226 to 44 and horizontal half-X outside 3..180 across edges, reverse topward motion belowY41, then advance the eight-frame phase.

If hunter Y exactly equals player Y, change horizontal delta to +/-4 towards player and stop vertical motion. Otherwise if their pre-move half-X values are exactly equal, choose vertical +/-2 towards player and stop horizontal motion. Nonaligned hunters keep their existing velocity.

On a changed pursuit direction play $346E with priority 6, release threshold 8 and sawtooth $20, preserving hunter X through $346B. Advance index until all $3454 active hunters processed; continuation jump at $3478 loops movement.
Number of awake hunters 0..3 and bomb-collection modulo 3 counter; three, six and nine collected bombs activate successive hunters.
Three signed Y deltas, initially+2; pursuit changes to 0,+2 or-2.
Three horizontal delta low bytes, initially 0, changed to 04 orFC while chasing on the same Y.
Three X delta high bytes, paired with $3459:00 for+4/zero,FF for-4.
Eight sprite pointers 10,11,12,13,14,15,12,16 forming the repeating hunter animation.
Three frame phases, six-call divider, saved hunter index, player half-X and current hunter half-X. Last two cache coordinates used by exact-alignment steering tests.
Envelope 10/C4 followed by frequencyC80A held 13 ticks twice, then 0; used each time exact alignment selects a new pursuit direction.
Branch-reach trampoline from $3451 back to hunter loop $3368 when more active hunters remain.
Unused loaded buffer residue after the final jump, entirely identical to corresponding tail of PLF01/02/04. No sprite-source overread occurs: all eight 30-byte frames are within $31D7-$32C6.
